rule: Skill and agent git and gh commands reference captured identifiers only as quoted shell variables and paste only gate-validated placeholders
description: `plugin/skills/push-branch/SKILL.md` requirement 2 is the source for the push command form that applies the Shell Identifier Discipline in `plugin/governance/security-policy.md`: the skill's push is one call to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/push-branch/scripts/push-branch.sh` whose only identifier arguments are the placeholders `<allowlist-validated-head>`, `<allowlist-validated-base>`, and `<allowlist-validated-remote>`, and the same span binds each placeholder to the input value that passed the input gate. The source pin is one span carrying that binding sentence and the invocation that uses it, so pasting a branch or remote literal into the invocation, replacing a placeholder with an unvalidated value, or deleting the binding to the input gate turns the suite red. The script reads the branch, commit, upstream, and push remote itself, in the same process as the push, and references them only as quoted shell variables. Six consumers pin the same discipline at the other named command forms. In `plugin/skills/open-plan-pr/SKILL.md`: the step 6 push, one span carrying the sentence that binds `<allowlist-validated-head>`, `<allowlist-validated-base>`, and `<allowlist-validated-remote>` to the `head`, `base`, and `push_remote` values that passed the input gate together with the script invocation that uses them; the step 7 `gh pr create --base <allowlist-validated-base>` clause binding that placeholder to the `base` value that passed the input gate; and the step 8 block, one span from the `n="$(gh pr view <allowlist-validated-pr-number> --json headRefName --jq '.headRefName')"` read through the head SHA and URL reads, the empty-read blocker, the head branch blocker that compares against the gated `<allowlist-validated-head>` placeholder, the SHA-mismatch blocker that compares against the gated `<allowlist-validated-commit>` placeholder, and the final `printf` that emits only captured variables. In `plugin/skills/create-working-branch/SKILL.md` requirement 3, one span carrying the sentence that binds each `<allowlist-validated-...>` placeholder to the value that passed the input gate or the checks in steps 1 and 2, together with the script invocation that passes `<allowlist-validated-base>`, `<allowlist-validated-working-branch>`, `<allowlist-validated-classification>`, `<allowlist-validated-trunk-freshness>`, and `<allowlist-validated-trunk>`. In `plugin/skills/gather-facts/SKILL.md` requirement 1, one span carrying the sentence that binds each `<allowlist-validated-...>` placeholder to an input value that passed the input gate, the conditions for passing `--remote` and `--ref`, and the script invocation that passes `<allowlist-validated-trunk>`, `<allowlist-validated-remote>`, and `<allowlist-validated-reference>`. In `plugin/agents/github-reviewer.md` step 7, the single push, one span carrying the script invocation with the `<allowlist-validated-working_branch>` and `<allowlist-validated-base>` placeholders and the fixed `origin` remote, and the rule that exit 1 returns `blocked`. Replacing any captured variable with a pasted literal, or a gate-validated placeholder with a raw value, turns the suite red. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these seven word sequences exist in these five named files; they claim nothing about meaning and nothing about what an agent actually runs. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a meaning inversion around the pinned bytes, such as surrounding prose that offers a pasted-literal alternative to a pinned command, is invisible; (2) the pins cover only the named forms: any other command in these files, or a new command added beside a pinned one, that pastes an identifier stays green; the push-branch script's own git commands are not pinned here (its upstream comparison, mode selection, and own-name refspec are pinned by the working-branch no-track fixture, and its behavior is asserted by `tools/test_push_branch.sh`), and the create-working-branch and gather-facts scripts' own git and gh commands are not pinned here (the create-working-branch script's no-track creation and upstream rule are pinned by the working-branch no-track fixture, and the two scripts' behavior is asserted by `tools/test_create_working_branch.sh` and `tools/test_gather_facts.sh`); (3) a NEW skill or agent that authors git or gh commands with pasted identifiers is an absence defect that no fixture in this directory can see, per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract, and no structural check for it exists in `tools/policy_check.sh`; (4) the pins prove the documented form exists, not that the executing agent runs it rather than a pasted variant; (5) the github-reviewer step 7 placeholders are tied to the gated inputs only by their names and by the github-reviewer input gate sentence pinned in the shell identifier discipline fixture, because the pinned span carries no sentence that binds them; likewise the open-plan-pr step 8 placeholders `<allowlist-validated-head>` and `<allowlist-validated-commit>` are tied to the gated `head` input and the gated step 6 commit only by their names, by the open-plan-pr input gate and commit gate sentences pinned in the shell identifier discipline fixture, and by an unpinned binding sentence; (6) the github-reviewer grant wording in `plugin/governance/safety-rails.md` is outside these pins.

source.pattern: Run the push script, where each `<allowlist-validated-...>` placeholder is the input value that passed the input gate. Pass `--remote` only when `push_remote` is provided: ```bash bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/push-branch/scripts/push-branch.sh --head <allowlist-validated-head> --base <allowlist-validated-base> [--remote <allowlist-validated-remote>] --on-reject block --no-upstream block

consumers.pattern: Place the working branch on its remote in ONE Bash call to the push-branch script, where `<allowlist-validated-head>`, `<allowlist-validated-base>` and `<allowlist-validated-remote>` are the `head`, `base` and `push_remote` values that passed the input gate. Pass `--remote` only when `push_remote` is provided: ```bash bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/push-branch/scripts/push-branch.sh --head <allowlist-validated-head> --base <allowlist-validated-base> [--remote <allowlist-validated-remote>] --on-reject warn --no-upstream origin
Run `gh pr create --base <allowlist-validated-base> ...`, where `<allowlist-validated-base>` is the `base` value that passed the input gate

n="$(gh pr view <allowlist-validated-pr-number> --json headRefName --jq '.headRefName')" p="$(gh pr view <allowlist-validated-pr-number> --json headRefOid --jq '.headRefOid')" u="$(gh pr view <allowlist-validated-pr-number> --json url --jq '.url')" [ -n "$n" ] && [ -n "$p" ] && [ -n "$u" ] || { printf 'blocker: could not read the PR head branch, head SHA, or URL' >&2; exit 1; } [ "$n" = '<allowlist-validated-head>' ] || { printf 'blocker: PR head branch does not match head' >&2; exit 1; } [ "$p" = '<allowlist-validated-commit>' ] || { printf 'blocker: PR head SHA mismatch, expected %s got %s' '<allowlist-validated-commit>' "$p" >&2; exit 1; } printf 'url: %s\nhead_ref_oid: %s\n' "$u" "$p"

Run the branch script, where each `<allowlist-validated-...>` placeholder is the value that passed the input gate or the checks in steps 1 and 2: ```bash bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/create-working-branch/scripts/create-working-branch.sh --base <allowlist-validated-base> --branch <allowlist-validated-working-branch> --classification <allowlist-validated-classification> --trunk-freshness <allowlist-validated-trunk-freshness> --trunk <allowlist-validated-trunk>

Run the facts script, where each `<allowlist-validated-...>` placeholder is an input value that passed the input gate. Pass `--remote` only when `remote` is provided, and one `--ref` per reference: ```bash bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/gather-facts/scripts/gather-facts.sh --trunk <allowlist-validated-trunk> [--remote <allowlist-validated-remote>] [--ref <allowlist-validated-reference>]...

push ONCE (batch only, never per fix) via `bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/push-branch/scripts/push-branch.sh --head <allowlist-validated-working_branch> --base <allowlist-validated-base> --remote origin`; exit 1 means return `blocked` (relay the blocker).
